findings.claim: The I3b tests' check that no position from the new element is saved before the reseek, `expect(savedAfter.map(call => call[1])).not.toContain(0)`, can never fail, because `write` is never called with 0.
findings.impact: The I3b clause 'never saves a position read from the new element before that' has no working test. A regression that saved a stale or new-element position after a src change would pass the suite.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/__tests__/VideoPlayer.src.test.tsx (I3b block, both tests) asserts only that 0 is absent. frontend/src/lib/playbackProgress.ts:105, :191 and :269 call `write` only after the `usable()` check (`value > 0`), so 0 cannot appear in saveProgress calls at all. In jsdom the old controller's teardown (playbackProgress.ts:264-275) reads currentTime 30 from the same reused <video> after its src changed and writes 30. The assertion accepts that.
findings.repro: Mutation in my head: make the new controller's first onTick write `mc.getCurrentTime()` without checking resumePending or the interval gate. That saves 30 (test 1) or 0→skipped, and the assertion `not.toContain(0)` still passes. Not run.

bucket_proposal.reason: No declared invariant is broken by the code. The test meant to guard I3b's last clause is vacuous, so it reads as if it covers the clause.

findings.proposed_fix: Assert on the exact saveProgress calls after the new controller is handed out, for example that none of them carry the pre-change position (30) or any position other than the reseek target. Alternatively, reset currentTime to 0 and duration to NaN on src change in the test, as a real load does, and assert no save before the seek.

findings.claim: The I5 clause 'a request to a matching path is sent to backendProxy whatever its query string' has no test. Only `isStreamPath` on bare pathnames is tested, and the query stripping in server.js is not exercised.
findings.impact: If server.js stopped passing only the pathname, for example by passing req.url, addon streams with a query such as `?v=` would silently take the stalling Next.js rewrite. No test would fail.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/__tests__/server-routes.test.ts:5-34 tests pathnames only. frontend/server.js:61 and :72 strip the query with `new URL(req.url).pathname` and route on it. server.js has no unit test and is unchanged by this diff.

potential_unspecified_behavior.behavior: Inside the native shell without src, an onError prop is forwarded to ShellVideoPlayer, which ignores it, so it is never called.
potential_unspecified_behavior.reason: No caller passes onError without src today. An addon always passes src, so nobody sees a silent drop in ordinary use.

potential_unspecified_behavior.behavior: On a src change under the same videoId, in a real browser the old controller's teardown save reads the new element's reset currentTime (0), so the last up-to-5 s of progress on the old source is not written.
potential_unspecified_behavior.reason: The spec states no caller changes src under one videoId, so this needs use that does not occur.

potential_unspecified_behavior.behavior: A whitespace-only src string is truthy, so it is used as the element source and selects the browser player inside the shell, instead of falling back like "".
potential_unspecified_behavior.reason: Only a malformed caller-supplied src triggers it, which is outside ordinary first-party use.

regression_risks: Existing FilePreview callers pass no src. `src` (undefined) is a constant extra dep of the controller effect and `src || getStreamUrl` keeps today's value, so there is no regression by reading.
The regex alternation is anchored by an outer group with ^ and $, so lookalikes such as trailing slash or extra segments stay on Next.js; the tests cover these.

React may synthetically bubble a <source> child's error to the video's onError. There are no <source> children here, only <track>, so this does not apply today. Adding <source> children later would change I4 behavior.

I4: two error events give two calls. A track error does not call onError (fireEvent error does not bubble). The no-onError case only checks that nothing throws.
